title: He made a sultan, then unmade him. Then he went to court | Folio 2 — The Honest Historian #Shorts
description:
So Ali came. He arrived in Herat at the beginning of November. The next morning, he went to court. He knelt, kissed the Sultan's hand, and offered rich gifts. Masud spoke with him for a long time, about his brother, about money, about the army. Then Ali was asked to wait in a side room. And there, Beyhaqi tells us, about thirty servants seized him, stripped him of his robe and his boots, and put him in heavy chains. His baggage train was plundered the same day. Masud, it seems, had learned a simple lesson. A man who can give away a throne once can give it away again. Beyhaqi does not cheer. He says that only God knows what was truly in Ali's heart. And he adds a warning to anyone who trusts this deceitful world, because fortune turns, and the man who stands highest is often the next to fall.

The full story: Folio 2: Two Brothers, One Throne — on our channel and on every podcast app.
